summary: Modular monolith Django on Azure Container Apps with Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server as the database in US; front end: Angular, React Native.

frontend.justification: Web: An opinionated, batteries-included framework that scales to large teams. Fit for this project: team.languages includes TypeScript; strong maintainability for Angular (priority 4); strong scalability for Angular (priority 3); strong security for Angular (priority 5). Mobile: Shares JavaScript/TypeScript skills and code with the web team. Fit for this project: team.languages includes TypeScript; strong time to market for React Native (priority 3); strong maintainability for React Native (priority 4); strong performance for React Native (priority 3).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 1.3 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.security (strong security for Angular (priority 5)).
Scored 0.8 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.maintainability (strong maintainability for React Native (priority 4)).

tradeoffs: Steeper learning curve and more boilerplate than React/Vue.
JS runtime adds memory overhead on very low-end phones.
Some native modules need a development build.

backend.justification: Ships auth, admin panel, ORM and migrations out of the box. Fit for this project: team.languages includes Python; strong security for Django (priority 5); well suited to healthtech projects; built-in admin/back-office screens.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 1.9 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to healthtech projects).
Scored 1.5 points lower: the team would have to learn C#; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes Python).
Excluded: Firebase (Google) lacks HIPAA attestation/BAA (compliance).

tradeoffs: Heavier per-request overhead than Go/Node for very high RPS.

database.choice: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server (East US)
database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: ACID transactions keep money/bookings consistent; strong security for PostgreSQL (priority 5); well suited to healthtech projects; strong maintainability for PostgreSQL (priority 4). Data stays in East US to satisfy data_residency=us.

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server (East US)
alternatives.why_not: Scored 2.4 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to healthtech projects).
Scored 5.1 points lower: time-series extension adds operations without a time-series need; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to healthtech projects).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.justification: Serverless containers on Azure. Fit for this project: multi-zone deployments for 99.95%; strong scalability for Azure Container Apps (priority 3); strong cost for Azure Container Apps (priority 3); strong performance for Azure Container Apps (priority 3).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 0.1 points lower: close runner-up; the chosen option combines better with the rest of the stack.
Scored 0.1 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.cost (strong cost for Azure Container Apps (priority 3)).

supporting.justification: Uses the backend framework's maintained auth library, so user data stays in your own database in US.

alternatives.why_not: Separate vendor with per-MAU pricing.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Hosted checkout keeps you in PCI DSS SAQ A scope; broad global payment methods.

alternatives.why_not: Enterprise minimums.
Fewer local methods.

tradeoffs: Gateway fees (~2% per transaction) are not part of the infra estimate.

supporting.justification: Clients upload directly with pre-signed URLs, so large files never pass through the API; objects are encrypted at rest and private by default.

alternatives.why_not: Fine for documents, poor as app storage.

tradeoffs: Needs lifecycle rules to control growth.

supporting.justification: Caches static assets and public media close to users and absorbs traffic spikes.

alternatives.why_not: Slower first loads for public pages and media.

supporting.justification: Runs inside the existing backend; a Redis adapter lets several instances share connections.

alternatives.why_not: Per-connection pricing for something the backend can do itself.

tradeoffs: Long-lived connections need sticky sessions or a pub/sub layer.

supporting.justification: Caches hot reads and sessions to hold p95=300ms, and doubles as the pub/sub and job-queue broker.

alternatives.why_not: No pub/sub or persistence, so it cannot double as a broker.
Every read hits the database at peak.

tradeoffs: Another stateful component to size and monitor.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (payment webhooks, notifications, image processing, scoring) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.justification: Free push delivery to Android and iOS (via APNs) for job updates and reminders.

alternatives.why_not: Costs per message and DLT templates.

tradeoffs: Notification payloads must not contain sensitive data.

supporting.choice: Azure Key Vault + Activity Log + Azure WAF
supporting.justification: Compliance controls for HIPAA, SOC2: encryption keys you control, no secrets in code, tamper-evident audit logs and a web application firewall.

alternatives.why_not: Auditors expect platform-level key management and logs.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.

alternatives.why_not: Self-hosted server to maintain.

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights + OpenTelemetry tracing + uptime checks and on-call paging
supporting.justification: Logs, metrics and traces stay in the same cloud and region as the data. 99.95% needs alerting that wakes someone up.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L3: ~60000 users, ~1500 peak concurrent, ~300 req/s at peak, ~3046.9 GB stored
Compute sized for at least two zones for 99.95% availability
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees, SMS and payment-gateway transaction fees

warnings.message: Upper estimate ($5719) exceeds the $3000 budget; watch usage as you grow.
Taking payments: use the gateway's hosted checkout/SDK so card data never touches your servers (PCI DSS SAQ A).
